headline: ✅ YESTERDAY'S ALARM IS OFF THE BOARD AND IT ENDED WELL: all three houses on the 12:30 buyer tour were HELD, and all three listing offices asked you for feedback inside ninety minutes of each other — which is the receipt that the tour happened, and three replies you now owe. 🔴 THE UNPAID BILL IS STILL WILLOW POINT: the two agents who walked it Saturday morning are now roughly forty-eight hours uncalled, and no feedback form is coming on that address, ever. 🔍 Nothing new landed on your own listings since Saturday afternoon — Ridge Trail's fifth tour is two days old with no read back.

hotSignals.signal: 🔥 THREE TOURS IN TWENTY-ONE HOURS ON A LISTING THAT HAD NEVER BEEN SHOWN. Lindsey H. of Epique walked it 9:00–9:30 Saturday morning; Anna C. of A Squared Properties walked it 12:00–12:30, booked only four hours ahead; a third agent booked 4:00 PM and cancelled ten minutes later. Two different brokerages inside one morning, on top of Friday's first-ever 4:30.
hotSignals.action: 🔴 A SECOND OVERNIGHT HAS PASSED AND NEITHER AGENT HAS BEEN CALLED — roughly forty-eight hours now, up from twenty-three yesterday. ⭐ No feedback form exists on this address and none is coming, because it has never sent a REQUESTED notice in its life; the phone is the entire loop here. 🎯 Ask each the same two questions: how did it show against what else they are seeing, and is the number right. 🔍 You now have new leverage for that call — their sellers' own buy side toured three houses yesterday, so both halves of this family's move turn on the same conversation.

hotSignals.signal: 🎉 IT CONVERTED. The showings on this address stopped mattering Sunday evening when the seller and the buyers agreed — price, concessions and both sides at two and a half — and the closing office opened the contract for signature at 8:06 this morning. This board's oldest live signal is now a deal.
hotSignals.action: ⚠️ THE CONTRACT IS STILL UNSIGNED AS OF THIS RUN. ⭐ A handshake on Sunday and an unsigned document on Monday is the most fragile state a deal ever occupies — the entire job today is getting signatures on it. 🔍 Also worth closing the loop with the buyer's agent, who asked for a status Friday night and was never answered; the answer is now a good one. ⚠️ These buyers must still close their own house first, so this is a contingency, not a closing.

hotSignals.signal: 🎯 A FIFTH SHOWING SATURDAY AT 3:00 PM from an agent who had never shown this house before — the first genuinely new eyes on it in a week, and it came one day after a fourth independent read called the price too high.
hotSignals.action: 🔍 THE READ HAS NOW BEEN OUTSTANDING TWO FULL DAYS. This address does return forms roughly half the time, so it is still an open question rather than a no — but the odds are falling and a direct call to that agent is the faster instrument now. ⭐ THE LEVER THAT IS NOT A PRICE CUT: the last read scored staging one out of five and named unknowns as the objection, and a pre-inspection is exactly what removes unknowns. 🎯 One named live buyer already put a specific number under the ask in writing and offered you the representation — that pair of facts is what moves an institutional seller.

hotSignals.signal: 🔥 THE ONLY UNQUALIFIED YES ON THIS BOARD. Amy G. of Ethos International filed it herself after her 8/15 showing: interested — YES, her buyers have just started looking, really like the house, and it sits at the TOP of their list. She also phoned from inside the house mid-showing, so a call to her is a returned call, not a cold one.
hotSignals.action: ⚠️ DAY NINE, AND THAT IS PAST THE WINDOW WHERE A MACHINE OUTREACH IS THE RIGHT INSTRUMENT — this is a human call now, and it is the single highest-value one on the showing board. ⭐ SHE LEFT PRICED RIGHT BLANK: the objection is unasked, not absent, so the whole call is asking it. 🔴 The basement lights she reported are still unanswered, and the seller is the only person who knows why they did not come on.

upcoming: ✅ SUN 8/23 — THE BUYER TOUR WAS HELD, ALL THREE HOUSES. 120 King Arthur Pl at 12:30, 116 Palm Dr at 12:45, 106 King Valley St at 1:15. ⭐ The proof is not a confirmation notice but the aftermath: all three listing offices sent FEEDBACK REQUESTED notices between 1:00 and 2:30 that afternoon, which no office sends for a tour that did not happen. 🔍 This retires two days of this board warning that none of the three doors was booked — they were booked, on a channel this feed could not see.

📝 YOU NOW OWE THREE REPLIES — one to each of those listing offices, all filed Sunday afternoon and all still unanswered. ⭐ These are not courtesy notes: your buyers are financed and toured three houses in one afternoon, so what you say back is the opening move in whichever one they want.
✅ SAT 8/22 3:00 PM — 2368 RIDGE TRAIL: HELD, and still the freshest event on your own listings. A first-time agent on this house, its fifth showing in thirteen days. 🔍 NO FEEDBACK YET, two days on.

✅ SAT 8/22 9:00 AM and 12:00 PM — 225 WILLOW POINT CIR: both HELD, both still uncalled roughly forty-eight hours later. Lindsey H. of Epique and Anna C. of A Squared Properties. No form is coming from this address.

❌ SAT 8/22 4:00 PM — 225 WILLOW POINT CIR: CANCELLED. Booked at 7:39 that morning and killed at 7:49, ten minutes later. ⚠️ Still worth one question to the seller: was anyone home, or did something at the house turn it away?

📭 NOTHING IS BOOKED ANYWHERE ON THE SELLER-SIDE FORWARD CALENDAR — not one confirmed future tour, walk-through, inspection or appraisal in this feed. Thirteen tracked listings, zero forward activity, including the $1,150,000 listing that has never had a tour booked at all.

⏰ FRI 8/28 4:00 PM — 195 LAKE VIEW CIR closes at the title firm's Moody office; they put that date in writing, so the 8/31 the brokerage system still prints is the lagging record. 🔴 Three items — survey, home warranty, septic and sewer inspection — have been unanswered since 8/20, and septic is the one with lead time.
📅 SAT 8/30 — 833 MADISON LN goes live. Six days to pre-book it, and the Willow Point weekend is the whole argument for doing so.

feedback.note: 🔴 THE HARSHEST FORM THIS LISTING HAS EVER TAKEN. Interested: No. Priced right: TOO HIGH. Staging: 1 of 5 — the worst score anywhere on this board. Verbatim: “Too much work and unknowns. Also — They really need a basement for tools not just finished space. It definitely needs cosmetic updates but its the question of everything else that's concerning. I would do a pre-inspection and address some of those issues.” ⭐ READ THE SECOND HALF, NOT JUST THE FIRST: she named a fix that is not a price cut. “Unknowns” is what a pre-inspection removes, and it is the cheapest lever on this file.
Interested: No. Priced right: TOO HIGH. The third independent read to argue the number, and the one that turned this from an opinion into a pattern.

🔴 THE MOST EXPENSIVE LISTING IN THE BOOK AND NOT ONE TOUR HAS EVER BEEN BOOKED ON IT. ⭐ The weekend sharpened the point: a $185,000 listing pulled three tours in twenty-one hours off the same machine that has never produced a single booking here. 🔍 The comp work puts the big-house ceiling in that zip near $950K unless acreage carries it, which makes the silence a pricing answer, not a marketing one.

Willow Point ran paid ads for three days with nobody in the door, then took three tours in twenty-one hours once the market found it. 🔍 The gap that costs money is between photos ready and booked, and it is entirely inside your control.

It is that the agent on the most expensive house you have toured this year has watched you ignore three requests, and you will want something from that office eventually. One paragraph closes it.
